bundle_parts: The displayed chapter for a canon/mixed row is its START chapter, not its end.

Start precedence: the record's OWN start (MangaMapping.start / start_chapter) wins whenever stated (a single-chapter episode states it too); then a span's first number ('119-127' → 119); derivation only when the start is genuinely unknown (bare end value).
Derived start = previous canon episode's end + 1, clamped to this episode's own end (one derivation path off the end-position curve).

The clamp IS the majority/sliver rule: when the previous episode ended mid-chapter leaving only scraps, the next full chapter is shown; when two episodes share a chapter (end(prev) = end(ep)) the shared chapter is shown.
The first canon episode starts at the entry's scope start (mangaStartChapter), not chapter 1.
Across a reorder boundary (different regime, or prevEnd > end) no start is derived → null; callers fall back to the row's own end value when one is known.
entries.notes: Rendering the start requires the ambiguity fix in MangaMapping.start (Sean's Gintama ep-35 report, 2026-08-24: an exact ch-86 record rendered as ch 48 because derivation walked backwards into a jumped block). The 'sliver' language does not appear in this home; the client calls it 'the majority rule'. WITNESSED by tests: mapping.position.test.ts 'canonEpStartCh — display shows the FIRST chapter animated' → 'derives start as the previous episode's end + 1', 'clamps the start to this episode's own end when both share a chapter', 'starts the first episode at the entry's scope start, not chapter 1'.

entries.statement: solvePosition — the unified position solve: one driver field (ep | vol | ch) resolves to a full position whose state is 'run' (aired), 'hatch' (manga_only tail) or 'out' (out_of_range), with filler/anime-only episodes carrying NO manga values.
bundle_parts: A non-integer or < 1 query value yields null (pending), not a fabricated position.
ch < scope start → 'out' with boundMsg 'ch {startCh}-{published}' (chapters before the scope belong to a predecessor series).
ch > published → 'out' with the same boundMsg and unit = aired + aheadUnits + 1.
ch ≤ covered → 'run': the episode whose confirmed chapter range contains ch wins; otherwise chToEp; type from the exact row else episodeTypeAt.
covered < ch ≤ published → 'hatch' with a unit proportional to the tail's pacing (aired when no tail).
ep ≤ aired and type filler or anime-only-canon → 'run' with noManga = true (vol/ch null by design).
ep ≤ aired with an exact record → START chapter per the first-chapter ruling; vol from chToVol(start) falling back to the record's volume.
ep ≤ aired without a record → canonEpStartCh estimate (null when none) and its volume.
ep > aired → 'hatch' projection when a tail exists and the projected chapter ≤ published; otherwise 'out' with boundMsg 'ep 1-{aired}'.
vol < scope start volume or > totalVolumes → 'out' with boundMsg 'vol {startVol}-{totalVolumes ?? ?}'; without a per-volume ratio → null.
vol → resolves as the volume's FIRST chapter (volStartCh) with chEnd = the volume's estimated last chapter, then solves as a chapter.
entries.notes: Interaction spec is cited as docs/components/map-lookup.md (not read; outside the brief). Vol-driven chapter resolution uses the ratio (perVol) even when volume boundaries exist — a second inconsistency with the boundaries-first rule (chToVol is boundaries-first, the vol→ch inverse is ratio-only).

Internal type string 'anime-only-canon' never reaches the user; the DB/types vocabulary ('anime-only-canon', manga_status 'anime_only', source_type 'original') vs the badge vocabulary ('anime_only', 'manga_only') is the rename surface.
